problem_text:
A manufacturing network aims to devise a strategy for curbing energy waste from several production facilities. Currently, no conservation measures are in place.

The operational profile of each facility is as follows:
* For Plant A, energy intensity coefficient is 2.399, output volume is 280.232.
* For Plant B, energy intensity coefficient is 2.681, output volume is 299.356.
* For Plant C, energy intensity coefficient is 0.59, output volume is 236.692.
* For Plant D, energy intensity coefficient is 0.671, output volume is 158.493.
* For Plant E, energy intensity coefficient is 2.078, output volume is 74.611.

To achieve conservation, several retrofit technologies are available, each characterized by a specific efficiency improvement:
* Implementing Technology1 improves efficiency by 39%.
* Implementing Technology2 improves efficiency by 20%.
* Implementing Technology3 improves efficiency by 54%.
* Implementing Technology4 improves efficiency by 34%.
* Implementing Technology5 improves efficiency by 18%.

Adopting a technology at a facility entails an incremental cost per unit of output. The cost matrix for all facility–technology pairings is provided below:

| Facility \ Technology | Technology1 | Technology2 | Technology3 | Technology4 | Technology5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plant A | 18.738 | 161.267 | 65.74 | 81.22 | 37.658 |
| Plant B | 110.922 | 117.526 | 160.579 | 42.297 | 25.004 |
| Plant C | 175.46 | 127.745 | 55.758 | 183.438 | 37.192 |
| Plant D | 97.618 | 58.256 | 58.512 | 11.786 | 162.88 |
| Plant E | 181.23 | 138.746 | 40.015 | 93.929 | 75.657 |

The network must decide which technologies to deploy at each facility (facilities may implement multiple technologies concurrently), and a facility may also operate with only partial conservation measures if required. The objective is to guarantee that the aggregate energy waste is diminished by at least a fraction P = 0.494 of the baseline amount, while minimizing the total expenditure.
